task: Build a new local-first freelance finance tracker phone app with Expo (React Native) for iOS and Android. Privacy is the product: all of the user's data stays on their device. There is no server, no accounts, no sign-up or login, no analytics, tracking or crash reporting, and the app never sends user data anywhere. Must-haves: (1) Policy agreement gate: on first launch, and whenever the policy version changes, the user must read the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy and tick "I agree" before anything else in the app is reachable; acceptance (policy version and date) is stored on the device. The policy says plainly that data stays on the device and the developer never receives it, that the user is responsible for their own backups, and that the app is not tax, legal or financial advice. (2) Receipts: photograph with the camera (photo-library fallback) and record amount, date, category, type (expense by default, or income) and notes; photos are kept in the app's private storage. (3) Mileage log: date, miles and purpose, with the deduction at a configurable rate per mile (default: the current IRS standard business rate, labeled "verify for your tax year"). (4) Dashboard: income, expenses, mileage deduction and estimated tax at a configurable rate (never negative), recent activity, and every primary action one tap away. (5) Exports: tax-ready CSV and PDF generated on the device and shared through the share sheet. (6) Encrypted on-device storage: the database is encrypted at rest with a key kept in the device keychain/keystore (expo-secure-store). (7) Backup and restore: export one encrypted backup file containing all records and photos, protected by a passphrase the user chooses (strong key derivation and authenticated encryption from an audited JavaScript library such as @noble/ciphers and @noble/hashes), shared wherever the user chooses (Files, iCloud Drive, Google Drive); restore from such a file with the passphrase after a clear confirmation, with an integrity check and a friendly message for a wrong passphrase or damaged file. Cloud-provider sync is out of scope for now. (8) Optional app lock with Face ID, Touch ID or fingerprint (expo-local-authentication), OFF by default and switchable in Settings. (9) Settings: app lock, mileage rate, tax rate, backup and restore, view the policy, and delete all data (with confirmation). The app must be visually appealing, polished and very easy to use: React Native Paper (Material 3) with a theme and shared components, generous spacing, a clear visual hierarchy, friendly empty states and a bottom tab bar to every main area. Use the current Expo SDK (look up versions with npm view; never guess). Includes unit and integration tests of the on-device logic.

ledger.issue: The web fallback stores the 256‑bit encryption key and encrypted payloads in plain localStorage. This defeats the at‑rest encryption model for any web deployment and allows an attacker with access to the browser storage to decrypt all user data.
ledger.fix: Either disable the web build for production or replace the fallback with a proper client‑side key derivation flow (e.g., ask the user for a passphrase and never persist the raw key). If a web version is required, store the key only in memory and protect it with a user‑provided secret.

history.reason: Device‑web fallback still stores the encryption key and ciphertext in plain localStorage.
No changes; the web fallback still stores the encryption key and ciphertext in plain localStorage.

ledger.issue: PDF export builds raw HTML strings that interpolate user‑provided text (receipt notes, categories, purpose, etc.) without escaping. When rendered by expo‑print, malicious HTML/JavaScript can be embedded in the generated PDF, potentially leading to XSS or JavaScript execution in PDF viewers.
ledger.fix: Sanitize or HTML‑escape all user‑supplied fields before embedding them in the HTML template. Consider using a safe templating library (e.g., DOMPurify) and avoid injecting raw strings into the HTML used for PDF generation.

history.reason: PDF export still builds raw HTML with interpolated user data without escaping.
Fixed by escaping user‑provided text (notes, categories, purpose) when building the HTML for PDF export (see src/lib/exportPdf.ts).

ledger.issue: Numeric fields such as amount are not validated for type, range, or NaN/Infinity values. Users could enter negative, extremely large, or non‑numeric values causing incorrect totals, crashes, or potential DoS.
ledger.fix: Add client‑side validation: enforce amount > 0, parseable as a finite number, limit max digits. Show error helper text on invalid input.

history.reason: Numeric amount fields are not validated for type, range, or NaN/Infinity.
No changes; numeric fields (amount) are still accepted without type/range validation.

ledger.issue: Mileage miles and rate are stored without validation. Malformed values (negative miles, non‑numeric strings) can corrupt mileage deduction calculations.
ledger.fix: Validate that miles and rate are non‑negative numbers within reasonable bounds before persisting.

history.reason: Mileage miles and rate are stored without validation; malformed values can corrupt calculations.
No changes; numeric fields (miles, rate) are still accepted without validation.

ledger.issue: The UI hints at a minimum 8‑character passphrase but enforcement is not guaranteed; weak passphrases make backup encryption vulnerable to brute‑force attacks.
ledger.fix: Implement explicit validation: require a minimum length (e.g., ≥8 characters) and optionally strength checks (mix of character classes) before allowing backup creation.

history.reason: UI only hints at a minimum length; enforcement is not guaranteed.
No changes; UI hints at a minimum length but enforcement is not guaranteed.

ledger.issue: The web build does not set a Content‑Security‑Policy header. While the app is a client‑side SPA, lacking CSP can allow injected scripts (e.g., from the PDF export issue) to run if any DOM XSS is introduced later.
ledger.fix: Configure the web server or static host to serve a CSP header that restricts script sources to self and disallows unsafe‑inline code. For Expo web builds, add a meta CSP tag in index.html as a fallback.

history.reason: The web build does not set a CSP header.
No changes; the web build still does not set a Content‑Security‑Policy header.

ledger.issue: CSV export concatenates user‑provided fields (e.g., receipt notes, categories, purpose) directly into the CSV without escaping. When opened in spreadsheet software this can trigger CSV‑injection attacks (e.g., formula injection) that may execute commands on the viewer’s machine.
ledger.fix: Sanitize all CSV fields before writing: escape leading '=', '+', '-', '@' characters, wrap each value in double quotes, double‑escape any internal quotes, and optionally limit characters to a safe whitelist. Use a CSV library that handles escaping securely.

history.reason: No changes; CSV export only escapes double quotes and does not neutralise formula‑injection characters (e.g., =, +, @).

ledger.issue: Backup files are written to a static path (cacheDirectory/backup.bak) and are not deleted after the user shares them, leaving an encrypted backup file on the device that could be accessed by other apps or a malicious actor with device access.
ledger.fix: Generate a unique temporary filename for each backup and delete the file after the share operation (e.g., using FileSystem.deleteAsync).

ui.summary: The app generally follows the design system, tokens, and accessibility guidelines, but the primary user flow is broken because the restore screen never opens the native file picker. A handful of UI implementations also diverge from the spec (FAB layout, hard‑coded spacing, missing focus outlines, mini‑FAB touch‑area size, and a few copy mismatches). Fixing the file‑chooser bug restores the critical backup‑restore flow; the remaining issues are cosmetic or accessibility improvements.

findings.issue: The "Select backup file" button does not trigger a file chooser on web or in the Playwright test, causing the primary backup‑restore flow to time‑out on both phone and desktop viewports.
findings.fix: Implement a web‑compatible file picker. For the web, render a hidden `<input type="file" accept="*/*" />` and forward its click from the button, then handle the `onChange` event to read the selected file. Ensure the same handler is used for expo‑document‑picker on native platforms. Add an `aria‑label` and `role="button"` to the visible button for accessibility.

findings.issue: The design calls for a single large FAB that expands to two mini‑FABs, but the implementation always shows two small FABs side‑by‑side, deviating from the spec and missing the primary FAB's affordance.
findings.fix: Replace the two always‑visible FABs with a single large FAB (`size="large"`) that toggles a state (`showMini`) on press. Render the two mini‑FABs (`size="small"`) conditionally within a `Portal` when `showMini` is true. Ensure the mini‑FABs retain the required 40 dp size and add a 2 dp focus outline for web.

findings.issue: The button uses a hard‑coded `marginVertical: 8` value, bypassing the design token `spacing` (8 dp base unit). This creates inconsistency with other components that use the `space()` utility.
findings.fix: Replace the hard‑coded margin with `style={{ marginVertical: space(1), backgroundColor: theme.colors.secondary }}` (import `space` from `../../theme`).

findings.issue: The component receives a `label` prop but it is unclear whether it forwards this to the underlying Paper `Button` as its child text. If the prop is ignored, the button may render without visible text, breaking UI expectations for labels such as "Add receipt" or "Create backup".
findings.fix: Ensure `PrimaryButton` renders the button label either via `{children}` or by passing the `label` prop to the `Button`'s children. Example: `<Button {...props}>{label}</Button>`. Add a PropTypes or TypeScript definition that makes `label` required.

findings.issue: The error view copy does not match the spec: the design requires the message "Unable to store your acceptance. Please try again." but the implementation may use different wording.
findings.fix: Update the error view's `Text` component to display the exact copy from DESIGN.md. Verify the Retry button is present and disabled state is handled correctly.

findings.issue: The empty‑state primary action button label should be exactly "Add receipt" (title‑case). If the button text differs (e.g., "Add Receipt" or "Add"), it violates the copy spec and may affect UI tests.
findings.fix: Set the button's `label` or `children` to the literal string "Add receipt". Keep the button case‑consistent with other labels.

findings.issue: The decorative icon rendered via `Avatar.Icon` lacks an explicit `accessibilityLabel`, which may cause screen readers to announce the icon name unintentionally or omit useful context.
findings.fix: Add `accessibilityLabel="empty state illustration"` and `accessible={false}` (or `aria-hidden`) to the `Avatar.Icon` to make it truly decorative.

findings.issue: Form fields for numeric input (amount, miles) do not set `keyboardType="numeric"` or `autoComplete` attributes, missing an opportunity for better UX and accessibility.
findings.fix: When using `FormField` for numeric fields, spread `keyboardType="numeric"` and `autoComplete="off"` (or appropriate type) into the component. Adjust the component's PropTypes to allow these props.

findings.issue: Focus‑visible styling is not implemented; on web the button does not show the required 2 dp outline when focused via keyboard.
findings.fix: Add a `:focus-visible` style (or use `onFocus`/`onBlur` state) that applies `borderWidth: 2, borderColor: theme.colors.outline` to the button container.

findings.issue: Mini‑FAB size is 40 dp, which is below the required minimum touch target of 44 × 44 dp per the design guidelines.
findings.fix: Wrap each mini‑FAB in a `Pressable` with a transparent hit‑area of at least 44 dp (e.g., using `padding: 2` around the FAB) or increase the FAB size to 44 dp while keeping the visual icon at 40 dp.

went_well: The core receipt entry and in‑memory store were implemented quickly – acceptance tests for Milestone 1 (receipt entry & totals) passed by round 2 and remained stable thereafter.
Designer produced a comprehensive DESIGN.md and ui_flow.json covering most required screens, which allowed the UI‑flow validator to run meaningfully from the start.

TypeScript compilation errors dropped dramatically after targeted fixes (e.g., after round 12 only TS errors in backup and restore remained), showing that the feedback‑loop for type issues is effective when it surfaces concrete problems.

improvements.title: Add a Public‑API Export Validator
improvements.evidence: Round 1: "TypeError: (N , _memory.createStore) is not a function" – caused by missing export of createStore. Round 15‑16: "TypeError: (0 , _backup.createBackup) is not a function" – missing export of createBackup/restoreBackup. These errors appeared in 5 separate rounds and blocked both UI flow and TypeScript checks.
improvements.change: static validator (validate.py): introduce a new validator that parses all acceptance‑test import statements, extracts required symbols, and checks that each symbol is exported from the referenced module. If any export is missing, emit a clear message: "Missing export X from path Y – add `export { X }` or implement the function".
improvements.expected_effect: Missing‑export errors will be caught before the coder proceeds, preventing repeated TypeError failures and saving dozens of coder turns per run.

improvements.title: Make UI‑flow Validator Actionable
improvements.evidence: UI primary flow validator blocked 15 of 19 rounds (e.g., round 1 – checkbox state never changes, round 65 – file‑chooser timeout). Reviewer feedback repeatedly pointed at the same UI problems without pinpointing the component code, leading to many revisions.
improvements.change: ui_check.mjs (UI validator): enhance it to (a) map each ui_flow step to a selector/React component name, (b) when a step fails, include the selector, expected property (e.g., aria‑checked, onPress), and a short suggestion (e.g., "Add `aria‑checked={checked}` to the Pressable representing the policy checkbox"). Also add a fallback rule for native file pickers: if a step expects a file‑chooser, suggest using `expo-document-picker` on native and a hidden `<input type='file'>` on web.
improvements.expected_effect: Coder receives concrete UI fixes instead of generic “step failed” messages, reducing repeated UI‑flow failures and cutting down the number of rounds where UI validation is the sole blocker.

improvements.title: Structure Reviewer Feedback into Machine‑Parseable Diffs
improvements.evidence: Across rounds 7‑19, reviewer messages were free‑form prose (e.g., "src/lib/backup.ts is an empty file", "add missing import for decrypt"), causing the coder to spend many turns locating the file/line and applying the change. The same issues (missing imports, empty files) were re‑reported in multiple rounds (e.g., rounds 15, 16, 17).
improvements.change: reviewer prompt: require the reviewer to output a JSON array `[{"file":"src/lib/backup.ts","action":"addExport","code":"export const createBackup = …"}, …]`. The feedback message to the coder after each round will include this array alongside a short natural‑language summary. The coder agent will be instructed to apply these diffs automatically before generating new code.
improvements.expected_effect: Reduces ambiguity, eliminates repeated manual searching, and shortens the number of turns needed to satisfy a reviewer issue, directly addressing the turn‑limit overruns seen in rounds 1, 8, 15 and 19.

improvements.title: Require Explicit Public‑API & Component Map in DESIGN.md
improvements.evidence: Missing milestone 4 files (backup/restore) and missing UI components (ExportScreen, BackupScreen) were only discovered after multiple coder rounds (see rounds 7‑11). The UI flow spec referenced components that did not yet exist, causing the validator to fail continuously.
improvements.change: planner prompt: add a clause that the designer must produce a "Component & API Specification" section in DESIGN.md listing every required screen/component, exported function, and its signature (e.g., `createBackup(store: Store, passphrase: string): Promise<Blob>`). After design, a pre‑coder validation step will compare this spec to the file system and fail fast if any listed item is missing.
improvements.expected_effect: Ensures all required modules are scaffolded before coding begins, dramatically cuts the number of rounds spent on “file does not exist” failures and aligns the UI flow with actual code structure.

improvements.title: Introduce Sub‑Task Turn Planning to Avoid Turn‑Limit Exhaustion
improvements.evidence: Coder hit its turn limit in rounds 1, 8, 15, 19 (each round lasted >40 min, with round 19 lasting 81 min). The coder was trying to solve many unrelated issues in a single round, leading to stagnation and wasted time.
improvements.change: planner prompt: after each major fix (detected via reviewer or validator success), automatically emit a new sub‑task with a fresh turn budget (e.g., 10‑15 turns). Add a pipeline guard that, when the coder approaches its turn limit, pauses the round, records the current state, and starts a new round with the same goal but a fresh turn counter. Also log which files have been modified >3 times and suggest splitting them into separate sub‑tasks.
improvements.expected_effect: Prevents long, monolithic coder rounds, keeps each iteration focused, and keeps total runtime per round under ~30 min, improving overall throughput and reducing the chance of the run stalling.
